title: Himesh Patel Expresses Desire for Classic Sherlock-Watson Dynamic in Enola Holmes Series
text:
After Enola Holmes 3's debut, Himesh Patel, who plays Dr. Watson, shares his wish to see a classic Sherlock-Watson story with Henry Cavill, highlighting the potential for future spinoffs or sequels amid the franchise's expansion and critical reception.
Following the release of Enola Holmes 3 on Netflix , one of the film's new stars has opened up about the future of Henry Cavill 's portrayal of Sherlock Holmes within the franchise.
While Millie Bobby Brown remains the central figure as the brilliant Enola Holmes, Cavill's legendary detective plays a crucial supporting role across the series. His journey continues in the third installment, which marked one of the most anticipated movies arriving on Netflix in July. Beyond this chapter, Himesh Patel, who steps into the iconic role of Dr. John Watson, has shared his thoughts on where the story could venture next.
In an interview with ScreenRant's Liam Crowley, Patel-who appeared as Watson in the post-credits scene of Enola Holmes 2 and has a more substantial role in the sequel-was asked about his aspirations for the franchise alongside Cavill. Patel expressed a strong interest in exploring a traditional partnership between Sherlock and Watson, stating: I would just want to spend more time with him. I'd love to do a classic Sherlock-Watson story with him. That'd be a lot of fun.
I think he's a fantastic actor. He seems like a lovely guy in the time I've spent with him. But what he's done with what you see of Sherlock in this movie is really special, and I really would love to spend more time with Henry and tell a thrilling story.
The duo of Holmes and Watson stands as one of the most celebrated in literary history, with legendary pairings over the years including Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce, Robert Downey Jr. and Jude Law, and Benedict Cumberbatch and Martin Freeman. In the Enola Holmes series, Watson's introduction was carefully paced. He was absent from the first film, where Sherlock engaged in sharp banter with his brother Mycroft, played by Sam Claflin.
In Enola Holmes 2, Enola herself orchestrated Watson's arrival at 221B Baker Street, recognizing her brother's need for companionship. Although Cavill's Sherlock and Patel's Watson do share moments in the third film, their screen time together is limited, as the plot separates them. The narrative centers on Sherlock's kidnapping just before Enola's wedding to Lord Tewkesbury, portrayed by Louis Partridge. Enola and Watson then join forces to rescue the captured detective, setting the stage for a potential deeper partnership.
The cast of Enola Holmes 3 also features Helena Bonham Carter as Eudoria Holmes, Sharon Duncan-Brewster as a formidable Moriarty, Jason Watkins as Brigadier Sampson, and Hattie Morahan as Lady Tewkesbury. Directed by Philip Barantini and written by Jack Thorne, the movie has garnered largely positive reviews from critics.
However, ScreenRant's own review offered a more mixed perspective, noting that the film begins to reveal the constraints of the series' concept as it delves further into the Sherlock Holmes mythos. As of now, Netflix has not officially announced whether Enola Holmes 4 will be produced or if a spinoff focused on Sherlock and Watson will move forward.
With Enola Holmes 3 streaming on Netflix, Henry Cavill's next major project is the live-action Voltron film, currently slated for a 2027 release. The broader landscape of upcoming Sherlock Holmes adaptations includes Prime Video's Young Sherlock for a second season, Sky Television's The Death of Sherlock Holmes, and Former Prodigy Media's Moriarty Rising: A Sherlock Holmes Tale, ensuring the detective's legacy continues across various platforms and interpretations
